name: Technological University Dublin
description: Technological University Dublin is Ireland's first technological university, formed in 2019 from the merger of Dublin Institute of Technology and the Institutes of Technology at Blanchardstown and Tallaght. It teaches across campuses at Grangegorman, Aungier Street, Bolton Street, Blanchardstown and Tallaght.
whyIncluded: TU Dublin is among the 10 universities in Ireland most chosen by international students (about 22% of its 19,095 full-time-equivalent students are international, THE World University Rankings 2027 data), per the FinexisEdu shortlist research of October 2026.

livingCosts.summary: TU Dublin's own 2026/27 estimate for a student living away from home in purpose-built student accommodation, for the 9-month academic year. Excludes tuition, flights, visas and insurance.
livingCosts.notes: TU Dublin Student Services 'Cost of Living Guide' 2026/27, students living away from home, monthly figures (9-month year): housing = Rent PBSA incl. service charge EUR 1,453 (EUR 13,081/yr; cheaper digs options are EUR 559 (5-day) and EUR 709 (7-day) per month); food EUR 205; transport = Travel EUR 48; personal = books & class materials EUR 78 + clothes/medical EUR 43 + mobile EUR 12.99 + social life/misc EUR 96 = EUR 229.99, rounded to 230. The guide's EUR 278/month 'Student Charge' (the EUR 2,500 student contribution paid by EU free-fees students) is excluded because non-EU students pay full tuition instead.

programmes.name: BSc Computer Science (TU856)
programmes.summary: Yearly tuition for international (non-EU) students for the 2026/27 intake. TU Dublin does not fix fees for the whole course, so later years may cost more.
programmes.notes: TU Dublin 'International Undergraduate Programmes 2026/27' summary booklet (linked from the international Fees & Funding page), Level 8 table, 'Fee Per Year' column: 'TU856 Computer Science, 4 years, Grangegorman, 13,500'. Booklet: international fees range EUR 12,500-21,750 depending on course; pay 50% to secure a place and the rest by 31 January. No separate compulsory student levy for non-EU students is listed in the booklet or on the Fees & Funding page, so compulsory fees are 0. No 2024/25 or 2025/26 non-EU figures were found on TU Dublin's site, so there is no fee history.
